full_judgment:
3. Defendant Nos. t Eastern Maritime and Trading Corporation filed written objection against the application for attachment before judgment. Defendant No. 1 denied their liability to pay to the plaintiff the amount claimed by the plaintiff. The defendant No. 1 submitted that defendant No. 1 had advanced U S. dollar 4,81,287.72 on account of various ships handled by the plaintiff as their agent from time to time and that the plaintiff did not render proper account of such amount. On this ground defendant No. 1 was compelled to terminate the agency. Defendant No. 1 also contended that defendant No. 1 is only a charterer of the Vessel M V. Haci Sefer Kalkavan and that under the charter-party agreement defendant No. 1 did not acquire the ownership or any transferable interest in the aforesaid vessel which cannot he made liable for a decree, if any passed in favour of the plaintiff against the defendant in the instant suit and that, therefore, the plaintiff's application attachment of the vessel before judgment is liable to be rejected. Defendant No. 1 also contended that the ingredients for attachment before judgment under Order 38 rule 5 C.P.C. are absent in the instant suit. 

 4. The learned Subordinate Judge has passed the following order observing inter alia: The said vessel is now under the control and custody of defendant Nos. 1 and 2 is discharging clinker at Chittagong Cement Clinker Grinding Factory Jetty at Chittagong Port. The defendant No.1 is the despondent owner and is going to discharge cargo by 19th January, 1984. The said vessel is not a foreign liner (i.e. it will not go from Port to Port as a conference liner) not it is a regular trade liner and the same has a charter plight and the said vessel after discharging cargoes will go back to its original destination. The defendant No. 1 to the knowledge of the plaintiff does not own, hold or possess any properties moveable or immoveable except the vessel as described in the schedule below as to satisfy the decree that may be passed against the said defendant. The defendant Nos. 1 and 2 will remove the said vessel from the local limits of the jurisdiction of this Court and if the defendant succeed in removing the vessel, the decree in the suit that may be passed against them for the amount claimed will be completely frustrated ... ... Para 4 of the application for attachment before the judgment consists of "the said vessel is not a conference liner nor is it a regular liner and the same (is) on a charter plight and the said vessel after discharging the cargo will go back to its original destination. "So it appears that that the vessel after discharging the cargo will go back to its original destination and will not remain on voyage from port to port. In the present case, admittedly, the defendant No. 1 has got no other property in Bangladesh. ... ... If the suit be decreed, and if the vessel in question leaves the port of Chittagong at the present stage, then the object of the money suit may be frustrated. 

 "5.—(1) Where, at any stage of a suit, the Court is satisfied, by affidavit or otherwise, that the defendant, with intent to obstruct or delay the execution of any decree that may be passed against him — (a) is about to dispose of the whole or any part of his property, or 

 (b) is about to remove the whole or any part of his property from the local limits of the jurisdiction of the Court, the Court may direct the defendant, within a time to be fixed by it, either to furnish security, in such sum as may be specified in the order, to produce and place at the disposal of the Court, when required, the said property or the value of the same, or such portion thereof as may be sufficient to satisfy the decree, or to appear and show cause why he should not furnish security.
